messages:
Mia Chen: heads up - after the calibration sweep for fp8/int4 kernels we saw a ~12% p99 spike on long-context inference. attaching profiler snippet below.
Raj Patel: which run id? can you paste perf counters and kernel choices?
Mia Chen: run 1849123321. model=redwood-l7b, quant candidates tried: fp8_v2, int8_hybrid, int4_packed. notable: KV cache hit rate dropped ~18% when int4 path selected.
Lisa Nguyen: that sounds like a KV layout / alignment problem — do you have the selector log?
Mia Chen: paste of profiler excerpt:
```
PROFILE run=1849123321
kernel_select: chosen=fast_gemm_fp8_v2 alt=int8_gemm_packed reason=latency_est
kv_store.layout=interleaved_v2
batching.window_ms=6 -> 12
kv_hits=0.82 -> 0.67
p99=74ms -> 84ms
```
Oliver Park: interleaved_v2 + int4_packed kernels have historically had stride/misalignment issues that force extra memcpy/copy paths. that would lower kv effective hitrate.
Marco Ruiz: I can repro with a microbench:
```bash
python tools/bench_kv.py --model l7b --kernel int4_packed --ctx 8192 --batch 16
```
infra-bot: deploy 1849123400 -> canary started (no failures).
Mia Chen: also observed a NaN spike on single-threaded calibration runs while estimating per-tensor scales for int4: sample dump:
```
tensor_scale=0.0
gemm_accum=inf
forward: softmax produced NaN
```
Raj Patel: if init_scale or calibration step produces zeros you can get division by zero or overflow during dequant -> accumulation. did smoothquant or per-channel calibs run?
Mia Chen: we ran smoothquant variant on the fp8 path and it suppressed NaNs but perf regressed ~5% (extra ops during preprocessing).
Lisa Nguyen: mitigation ideas: clamp scales with min=1e-3; per-channel calibration; prefer fp8 for seq>2048 and int8 for short contexts based on measured crossover; force compact KV layout for int4 kernels.
Oliver Park: concrete selector change: if kv_layout=interleaved_v2 and kernel=int4_packed -> set force_copy=true and limit batching.window_ms<=8. that should avoid the slow path at cost of extra CPU copy.
Mia Chen: that might reduce p99 but increases CPU copy time and could affect throughput.
Marco Ruiz: proposal: AB test combo = (selector tweak + clamp scales + smoothquant fallback on NaN). gather telemetry: kv_hits, p99, cpu_copy_ms, nan_rate, tail_latency.
Lisa Nguyen: +1. also add a micro-profiler hook to log scale_hist and count zero/near-zero scales at calibration. small change but high signal.
Mia Chen: I'll draft the selector + clamp change and push to canary tomorrow. will include bench script and numbers. ping me if you want to pair on perf runs.
Raj Patel: can someone ping @eng-sre to add alerts for NaN spikes and quantized-route p99?
eng-sre: noted — we will add alerting: quant_nan_rate > 0.5% and baseline_p99 regression > 8% over 1h window.
Mia Chen: thanks, will link PR and bench results here once ready. :thumbsup:
